fatal_errors: Machine learning is presented as the surface-modification method, but no physical coating or treatment selected by the model is specified.
The central intervention—atmospheric plasma spraying of an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating followed by annealing at 550 °C for 2 h—is absent.
The claimed 25% improvement and corrosion-rate thresholds are fabricated and unsupported by measurements or cited evidence.
The relevant electrochemical and high-temperature molten-salt exposure conditions are omitted.
No acknowledgment is made that the source article was retracted and its results require caution.
explanation: The hypothesis only aligns with the broad goal of improving stainless-steel corrosion resistance through surface modification. It does not reconstruct the actual method, materials, annealing condition, environments, or reported outcomes. Its generic passive-layer mechanism has limited conceptual relevance, and the unmodified-steel baseline is reasonable but underspecified. The proposed test could detect corrosion broadly, yet it lacks defined steel grade, exposure medium, coating, controls, and validated thresholds. With no supporting evidence and invented quantitative claims, it is unsupported rather than a plausible reconstruction.
